description: The bar chart illustrates the token count for two distinct components—“Reasoning” (orange) and “Demonstration” (blue)—across varying numbers of shots (0 through 4), as part of an analysis from the paper “Mapping the Minds of LLMs: A Graph-Based Analysis of Reasoning LLM.” The vertical axis represents “Token Count,” ranging from 0 to 7000 in increments of 1000, while the horizontal axis indicates the “Number of Shots,” labeled 0 to 4. At 0 shots, only the “Reasoning” component is present, with a token count of 6393. Starting at 1 shot, each bar becomes a stacked bar: the lower orange portion represents “Reasoning,” and the upper blue portion represents “Demonstration.” Red downward arrows with negative values (–1952, –1613, –1040, –1379) are annotated above the stacked bars for shots 1 through 4, indicating the reduction in “Reasoning” token count relative to the 0-shot baseline. The “Reasoning” portion decreases with increasing shots, while the “Demonstration” portion increases, suggesting a trade-off in token allocation as more examples (shots) are introduced. The chart visually emphasizes how the model’s internal token budget shifts from pure reasoning to incorporating demonstration examples as shot count increases.
